investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on 2-Node Subset
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-31T11:11–11:19Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted across the two eligible nodes (0/2 had sufficient capacity) and the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. As a direct consequence, the agent VM was never provisioned, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completed successfully, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were absent from the probe result. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on all eligible nodes (0/6 nodes available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector). As a result, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable for ~142–149 seconds before the eval times out, and the runner never reaches the state-polling logic that would produce the required evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool in production-api; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader service incident is present in the packet.

investigation.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI Billing Hard Limit Reached on /api/generate/image/stream
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API returned a hard billing limit error (billing_hard_limit_reached) when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream. The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of a generation_completed frame, causing both required contract assertions to fail: frameTypes did not contain "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent remained false.
investigation.rootCause: The OpenAI account used by the eval runner has hit its configured billing hard limit. When the eval probe at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1984) called /api/generate/image/stream, the upstream OpenAI image generation API rejected the request with error code billing_hard_limit_reached. The server translated this into a generation_error SSE frame (GENERATION_FAILED) and the stream never emitted a generation_completed frame or an image artifact URL. This is an external dependency (billing/quota) failure surfaced through the eval, not a code defect in the eval runner or contract definition. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval infrastructure failure.

investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot itself is structurally valid and was produced by github-actions (evidence: failed-check.evidence), but it is 612 minutes old at the time of the eval run (2026-07-31T11:19:10.340Z), meaning the last successful publish occurred roughly 10 hours and 12 minutes before the check ran. The contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 requires snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300; the observed value of 612 violates that assertion directly. This is an eval-detected staleness condition scoped to the snapshot publishing pipeline; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

A repository or Pages configuration change caused the published URL (https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json) to serve a cached or stale version despite a newer artifact being available.

investigations.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI Billing Hard Limit Reached on /api/generate/image/stream
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API returned a hard billing limit error (billing_hard_limit_reached) when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream. The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of a generation_completed frame, causing both required contract assertions to fail: frameTypes did not contain "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent remained false.
investigations.rootCause: The OpenAI account used by the eval runner has hit its configured billing hard limit. When the eval probe at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1984) called /api/generate/image/stream, the upstream OpenAI image generation API rejected the request with error code billing_hard_limit_reached. The server translated this into a generation_error SSE frame (GENERATION_FAILED) and the stream never emitted a generation_completed frame or an image artifact URL. This is an external dependency (billing/quota) failure surfaced through the eval, not a code defect in the eval runner or contract definition. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval infrastructure failure.

failed-check.evidence: imageUrlPresent = false, violating the contract assertion at expected-output.contract (imageUrlPresent must equal true).

possibleCauses: Primary: The OpenAI account (or API key) used by the eval runner has reached its billing hard limit, causing all image generation requests to be rejected immediately with billing_hard_limit_reached. This is the most strongly supported cause given the explicit error code in failed-check.message.

investigations.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returns 502/424 provider_account_unavailable
investigations.summary: The model-matrix eval failed because exactly one of two configured models, aura-gpt-5-5, returned a 502 bad-gateway wrapping a 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable. The other model, aura-claude-sonnet-4-6, passed cleanly. This is a localized eval failure against the aura-gpt-5-5 runtime path; no sibling checks failed and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The AURA backend was temporarily unable to reach the upstream model provider for aura-gpt-5-5 at the time of the eval run (2026-07-31T11:11:00Z). The runtime endpoint POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test returned HTTP 502 containing a nested 424 Failed Dependency with code provider_account_unavailable and the message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits." The error is explicitly scoped to the provider connectivity layer on AURA's side, not to eval infrastructure, credentials, or the aura-claude-sonnet-4-6 path. Because no prior run history exists (previousRunCount=0) it is unknown whether this is a new regression or a pre-existing intermittent condition.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on 2-Node Subset
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-31T11:11–11:19Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted across the two eligible nodes (0/2 had sufficient capacity) and the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. As a direct consequence, the agent VM was never provisioned, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completed successfully, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were absent from the probe result. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
